idiom_name: Vue 3 ref()/reactive() proxies + template bindings (v-model, @click, computed)
implementation_notes: Vue's reactivity system is the modern MVVM binder: ref() wraps a value in an object whose .value getter/setter track reads and trigger re-renders, reactive() makes plain objects proxies, and templates unwrap refs automatically, so component state and the DOM bind declaratively (v-model for two-way editors, @click for commands). Tracking happens inside getters and setters, which is why state must be accessed through the reactive wrapper - the original object stays non-reactive. Prefer computed() for derived view state so it is cached and recomputed only when its dependencies change.
pitfalls: Destructuring a reactive object or extracting a plain property loses reactivity; keep the object whole or use toRefs().
Replacing the raw object behind a nested reference breaks the Proxy link: always mutate through the reactive proxy (this.someObject !== newObject in Vue 3).
v-model writes into state on every keystroke; put validation in computed values or guarded setters, not in the template.
Watchers and standalone effect scopes created outside a component keep running unless stopped - a silent leak.

variants.name: MobX annotated observable view-model
variants.implementation_notes: MobX makes an explicitly annotated view-model observable: observable fields, computed getters, action methods, and reactions (autorun/reaction) push changes into whatever view layer consumes the state - an annotation-driven binder with precise dependency tracking that is independent of the framework. Use it with React or plain DOM when you want one testable view-model object rather than component-local state: makeAutoObservable infers the annotations, makeObservable is the explicit form called in the constructor.
pitfalls: makeObservable must be called unconditionally in the constructor and only supports already-defined fields; a missing call leaves the object silently unobservable.
Class fields compiled with modern decorators/definite-assignment interact badly with make(Auto)Observable unless the build configuration matches MobX's requirements.
Annotating the same field twice, or mixing decorators and annotations in one inheritance chain, throws at runtime.
MobX tracks through property access: values passed out of the observable tree (to a non-reactive widget or a worker) lose tracking - convert deliberately with toJS().
